title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the sequel to La Longue Marche (c. 1981). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite free group on l_0 and l_1, with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, and ρ is the symmetry exchanging l_0 and l_1. Π̂_{0,3} sits inside a larger profinite group Ŝ^+_{0,3}, which contains a square root ε_0 of l_0 (since l_0 = ε_0^2 is used) and an element σ_∞ of order 2. A plausible but unconfirmed reading is a profinite PSL_2(Z)-type orbifold group containing Π̂_{0,3} as a Γ(2)-like subgroup, with ε_0 playing the role of T and σ_∞ that of S. The map φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a homomorphism with φ̂(l_0) = ε_0 and φ̂(l_1) = σ_∞ (up to the sign σ_∞^{-1} = σ_∞). An element u of the group M^{!~}_{0,3} of 'automorphisms' is described by invariants g, h, f, γ, β_0, α, β, ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ_∞ρ(β)^{-1} (§46). The previous page reduced the condition 'u commutes canonically with φ̂' (relation (5)), case by case on the generators, to two facts: λ = φ̂(f)^{-1}ε_0^r f (relation (6)), and a condition on φ̂(ξ).

Theorem on this page. u commutes canonically with φ̂ iff φ̂(ξ) = ε_0^r β σ_∞^i for some r ∈ Ẑ and i ∈ Z/2 (relation (7)). λ is then given by (6). In the margin: r and i are uniquely determined once α and β are chosen.

Dependence on choices. u determines (α, β, f) only up to (α, β, f) ↦ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β, l_0^n f), n ∈ Ẑ (relation (8)). Under this change:
- ξ' = l_0^n ξ l_1^{-n};
- hence φ̂(ξ') = ε_0^n φ̂(ξ) σ_∞^n;
- using β' = l_0^n β = ε_0^{2n} β and comparing with (7) gives r' = r − n and i' = i + n mod 2 (relation (9)).

The point of (9) is the next page's corollary. Taking n = r gives a unique 'normalized' triple with φ̂(ξ) = β σ_∞^i. The u commuting with φ̂ then correspond bijectively to triples satisfying the loop equation ξ ≐ η l_1^ν together with this normalization. This is a step in describing the 'symmetrized' version of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group: elements compatible with the extra orbifold symmetries.
errors: The value of λ is written as φ̂(f)^{-1} l_0^r f, whereas (6) on the previous page has ε_0^r. Since l_0 = ε_0^2, these differ; it is probably a slip, with ε_0^r intended.

The exponent label in (7) is written variously as i, α and \dot α (the domain is 'α ∈ Z/12Z' in the image, presumably meaning Z/2Z). This is a notational slip only, in conflict with the element α ∈ Π̂.
Mixed notation for σ_∞^{±n} in the image ('σ_∞^{-n}' in the margin computations); it is harmless because σ_∞ has order 2.

Uniqueness of (r, i) (the NB) is asserted without proof. It needs that a conjugate of a nontrivial power of ε_0 is never a power of σ_∞, which holds in a free profinite product Ẑ * Z/2 type structure but is not argued here.
The computation itself, (8) ⇒ (9), checks out: ε_0^n φ̂(ξ) σ_∞^n = ε_0^{r'} ε_0^{2n} β σ_∞^{i'} gives φ̂(ξ) = ε_0^{r'+n} β σ_∞^{i'-n}, hence r' = r − n and i' = i + n.

ideas.what: Criterion for an automorphism u (given by loop-equation invariants) to commute with the 'half' homomorphism φ̂: Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} (l_0 ↦ ε_0, l_1 ↦ σ_∞): φ̂(ξ) = ε_0^r β σ_∞^i.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT-type elements with the S_3 / orbifold (PSL_2(Ẑ)-type) symmetries of M_{0,3}; 2-cycle relation of Ĝ T
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for the GT relations; Lochak–Schneps for refinements
ideas.where_published: Only the general program appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this computation is in unpublished Longue Marche sequel notes.

ideas.what: Ambiguity of the triple (α, β, f) under left multiplication by l_0^n, and normalization of the triple (r = 0) using the transformation law r' = r − n, i' = i + n.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of the parameter of a GT element (choice of f in the centralizer coset; cf. f ∈ F̂_2' normalization)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, correct bookkeeping step inside Grothendieck's unpublished 1981 study of the 'loop equation' (an early form of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations). It is of historical interest as a pre-Drinfeld treatment of normalizing GT-type parameters with orbifold symmetries, but contains no result beyond what the later GT literature covers.
transcription_corrections: The value of λ in the image reads 'λ = φ̂(f)^{-1} l_0^r f' (with l_0, not ε_0), as transcribed. This conflicts with (6) on the previous page.
The domain of the exponent in (7) is written 'α ∈ Z/12Z' in the image, presumably meaning Z/2Z for the exponent i (\dot α).
In the computation of φ̂(ξ'), the image shows φ̂(l_0^n)φ̂(ξ)φ̂(l_1^{-n}) = ε_0^n φ̂(ξ) σ_∞^{-n}, with crossed-out text beneath.
The intermediate line reads φ̂(ξ) = ε_0^{r'-n} β' σ_∞^{i'-n}; the 'r'−n' is overwritten in the image.
